body:
E-liquid keeps for a long time when it is stored well, and goes off surprisingly quickly when it is not. Heat, light and air are its enemies. A bottle left on a sunny windowsill or in a hot car can darken, lose flavor and turn harsh within weeks, while the same bottle kept cool, dark and capped can stay good for many months. Storage is also a matter of responsibility: liquid contains nicotine and must be kept away from children and pets. This guide explains how to store e-liquid for freshness, what temperature and light to avoid, how to handle open and unopened bottles, how to organize stock, how to carry small bottles, how long liquid lasts, how to tell when it has gone off, how to dispose of old liquid and how to keep everything out of reach. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## Why storage matters
E-liquid is a mix of propylene glycol, vegetable glycerin, flavorings and, in most products, nicotine. Heat speeds up chemical changes that dull flavor and darken the liquid. Light, especially sunlight, breaks down flavor compounds and nicotine. Air, if a bottle is open or half empty with the cap off, oxidizes the liquid. Good storage slows all three. See [e-liquid ingredients explained](/blog/e-liquid-ingredients-explained/).

## Keep it cool
Store liquid at room temperature or a little cooler, ideally between about 50 and 70 degrees Fahrenheit. A kitchen cupboard away from the oven, a drawer in a bedroom or a cabinet in a hallway is usually fine. Avoid hot cars, windowsills, shelves above radiators and places near heaters. Heat is the single biggest cause of liquid going off. Do not freeze liquid, because freezing can cause separation, though a cool fridge is acceptable if you wish and allow the liquid to warm to room temperature before use.

## Keep it dark
Light breaks down flavor and darkens liquid. Many bottles are tinted to help, but do not rely on that. Store them in a closed cupboard, or in their original box. Keep them away from direct sunlight and bright indoor lights.

## Keep the cap tight
Close the cap firmly after each use. An open bottle lets in air, which oxidizes the liquid, and lets flavor escape. If the bottle has a child-resistant cap, make sure it clicks shut. A tight cap also prevents spills and leaks, and keeps the bottle out of curious hands.

## Store upright
Keep bottles upright, so that liquid does not sit against the cap and seep. If a bottle leaks, wipe it, check the cap and replace the bottle if the dropper is damaged. For bottles with a dropper tip, keep the tip clean.

## Opened versus unopened bottles
Unopened bottles keep longest, so store extras sealed. Opened bottles are exposed to air each time, so use them within a reasonable time, and keep the cap tight. If you open a large bottle, consider pouring a little into a small, labelled refill bottle for daily use, and keep the large one closed. See [e-liquid bottle sizes](/blog/e-liquid-bottle-sizes-30ml-60ml-100ml/).

## How long does liquid last?
Most liquids have a best-by date of one to two years from manufacture, printed on the label or the box. Properly stored, they can stay good for much of that time. Nicotine liquids may darken with age, and flavor can fade. Fruit and menthol flavors tend to fade sooner, and dessert and tobacco flavors often hold up well or even improve slightly over a short period. See [e-liquid shelf life and expiry](/blog/e-liquid-shelf-life-and-expiry/) and [what is steeping](/blog/what-is-steeping-and-does-it-matter/).

## Signs liquid has gone off
- **A very dark color** much darker than when you bought it.
- **A sour, harsh or chemical smell.**
- **A flat or off taste.**
- **Separation,** with layers or particles in the bottle.
- **A thick, syrupy texture** that does not return to normal at room temperature.

If you see these signs, do not use it. Dispose of it responsibly.

## Organizing stock
Label the date you bought or opened each bottle, with a marker or a sticker. Keep older bottles at the front and use them first. If you have several flavors, keep them together, and check the dates monthly. A small box or tray keeps bottles tidy, upright and easy to find. Do not buy more than you will use before the dates, as explained in [bulk buying tips](/blog/bulk-buying-vapes-save-money/).

## Carrying liquid
Carry small bottles in a sealed bag, upright, in a pocket or bag away from heat. For travel, use bottles of 3.4 ounces (100 mL) or less in a clear bag. Pressure changes can cause leaks, so tighten caps and keep the bag upright. See [traveling with vapes](/blog/traveling-with-vapes-airline-rules/) and [best vapes for travel](/blog/best-vapes-for-travel/). Do not carry liquid loose in a pocket with keys.

## Keeping liquid away from children and pets
E-liquid contains nicotine, and a small amount can be dangerous to children and pets. Store bottles in a closed cupboard, ideally a lockable one, out of reach and out of sight. Keep the original packaging and child-resistant cap. Do not decant liquid into food or drink containers. Wipe spills at once. If a child or pet is exposed, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 or a veterinarian immediately. See [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/).

## Disposing of old liquid
Do not pour liquid down the drain or onto the ground. Absorb small amounts with cat litter or paper towels, seal in a bag and take it to a hazardous waste site. Empty bottles still contain residue, so keep them out of reach and dispose of them according to local rules. See [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/).

## A worked example
You buy three 30 mL bottles. You write the date on each, put two in a cupboard away from the stove and keep one in a bag for daily use. You use the bag bottle, wipe the tip and tighten the cap each time. When it is empty, you open the next oldest. After six months, the last bottle still tastes good, because it was kept cool, dark and sealed. If you had left it on a sunny windowsill, it would have darkened and lost flavor in a few weeks.

## Common mistakes
- **Leaving bottles in a hot car.**
- **Storing on a windowsill.**
- **Leaving caps loose.**
- **Buying more than you can use.**
- **Decanting into unlabelled containers.**
- **Leaving bottles where children or pets can reach them.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I keep liquid in the fridge?
A cool fridge is acceptable, but not necessary. Let it warm to room temperature before using, because cold liquid is thick.

### Does shaking a bottle help?
A gentle shake before use mixes the contents. Do not shake vigorously.

### Why did my liquid change color?
Nicotine liquid darkens with age and air. A little is normal. A very dark liquid may be past its best.

### Can I store liquid in the tank?
Not for long. Liquid in a tank is exposed to air and heat. Empty it if you will not use the device for a while.

### Is it fine to mix old and new liquid?
Better not. Finish old bottles first, and keep flavors separate.

## Shop
Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Storing different types of liquid
### Nicotine salts
Salts are generally stable. Keep them cool and dark, and tighten the cap. They tend to darken slowly, which is normal.

### Freebase
Freebase liquids oxidize and darken a little faster. Keep large bottles tightly capped, and consider decanting into a smaller bottle for daily use.

### Zero-nicotine and shortfills
Without nicotine, liquid darkens less, but flavor still fades with heat and light. Treat them the same way.

### Dessert and fruit flavors
Dessert flavors often hold well, while delicate fruit and menthol flavors fade sooner. Use fruit and menthol liquids earlier, and keep them especially cool.

## Common storage places, rated
- **Closed kitchen cupboard away from the oven:** good.
- **Bedroom drawer:** good.
- **Bathroom cabinet:** not ideal, because of humidity and temperature swings.
- **Car glove box:** poor, because of heat.
- **Windowsill:** poor, because of light and heat.
- **Fridge:** acceptable, but unnecessary, with a warm-up before use.

## A monthly check
Once a month, look at your bottles. Check dates, colors and caps. Wipe any sticky residue from the outside. Move the oldest bottles to the front. Dispose of any that look or smell wrong. A five-minute check keeps stock fresh, and it is a good moment to confirm that everything is out of reach of children and pets.

## What to do if you are away
If you will be away for a long time, empty tanks and pods, cap bottles tightly and store everything in a cool, dark cupboard. Do not leave liquid in a device. If you return after months, check the dates and the condition before use.

## Questions about storage
### Can I store liquid in the bathroom?
It is not ideal, because humidity and temperature swing. Choose a cupboard in a cooler, drier room.

### Does a tinted bottle mean I can leave it in the light?
No. Tinted bottles help, but light and heat still degrade liquid. Store them in the dark.
